To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glaciofluvially deposited sediments and landforms on Victoria Island record a complex meltwater regime and ice-sheet dynamics.

1) the glaciofluvio-sedimentary system of the Victoria Island is composed by tunnel channels, eskars, fans and extended deposits, and 2) the morphology of tunnel channels is the result of catastrophic meltwater flows, whereas eskers and their associated deposits are indicative of a seasonal meltwater regime.

the channelized glacio-fluvial system on Victoria Island, Northwest Territories is interpreted to have formed in an environment of thin ice with a grounding-line, and that subglacial meltwaters were seasonally controlled and episodic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the glacial history of the Victoria Island area, the glacial dynamics of the region and the nature and extent of the subglacial melt water system during the late Wisconsin glaciation.
the reconstruction of the Quaternary history of Victoria Island, and the interpretation of this history in terms of the regional and global climate and the regional and global tectonic setting.
the glaciofluvio-sedimentological record of glacioflual processes on Victoria Island, Northwest Territories.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glacial and glaciofluvially deposited sediments and landforms on Victoria Island provide a detailed and integrated record of ice-sheet dynamics and the subglacial melt-water regime.
it has shown the value of combining sedimentological, geomorphological and glaciological techniques to provide a more complete understanding of the processes that shaped the landscape.
we are looking at the sedimentology of glacial meltwater deposits and how they can be used to understand ice sheet processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tunnel channel and esker are products of catastrophic subglacial melt water flow, and that the tunnel channel is the product of a catastrophic subglacial flow in a combined channel (ice – substrate) and not in a simple R-channel.
there is an opportunity to use the geomorphology of these glaciofluvially formed features as a proxy to infer the subglacial melt regime and dynamics of the ice sheet.
the ice-sheet dynamics and sub-glacial melt-water regime can be inferred from form and sediments of glacioflvial systems.
